title: BADAN JSON export bundle
description: The v1.0 JSON bundle envelope (execution plan §22.2). This is the PUBLIC face of an export: snake_case keys, ISO-8601 timestamps with a numeric offset, raw and derived in physically separate arrays (I5). BADAN's internal storage is unchanged by this schema — timestamps are epoch-millis in SQLite and are rendered on the way out; do not read this file as a description of the database. Written as a real JSON Schema rather than prose so a downstream consumer can validate a bundle mechanically; scripts/gen_data_dictionary.py reads it to generate DATA_DICTIONARY.md.

export_schema_version.description: Semver of the export contract this bundle was written against. Additive changes bump the minor, breaking changes bump the major with migration notes in CHANGELOG.md.

dictionaries.description: Self-description of the ids used in this bundle, derived from the bundle's own contents so the artifact stays readable without the app, the registry, or a network. Every array is sorted by its own id for byte-stability.

canonical_unit.description: The unit every value for this metric is stored and published in.

appears_in.description: Which top-level arrays carry rows for this metric.

algorithms.description: Every algorithm that produced a derived value or baseline in this bundle, with the versions actually present. Two versions of one algorithm appearing together is normal and expected: derived values append, never overwrite (I2).

raw_samples.description: As-measured readings (I1: each carries full provenance). Never contains a computed value — see derived_values.

interval_records.description: Normalized aggregates over a window (daily steps, nightly time-asleep). Measured-derived, not engine-computed: is_derived is false and value_type is 'aggregate'.

sessions.description: Sleep episodes. Workout episodes are NOT here — they are promoted to `workouts` as parent objects and are not duplicated.

workouts.description: Workout episodes as parent objects with references, never flattened. A workout's heart-rate series is referenced by query descriptor into raw_samples, never copied.

derived_values.description: Engine-computed values. Physically separate from raw (I5) and self-documenting: every row names the algorithm and version that produced it.

logs.description: User-entered structured logs, kept apart from the measurement chain. `symptoms` and `adherence` are sensitive-class (I7) and appear only under an explicit includeSensitive scope. `hydration` is normal-class (a logged drink is the user's own data, never paywalled) and appears in a DEFAULT export, but is added ONLY when the export caught at least one drink — an install without the module, or an export whose scope caught no drinks, omits the key entirely rather than emitting an empty block that would assert 'this user logged no drinks'. `journal` is reserved for EPIC-29 and is deliberately absent rather than emitted empty — an empty array would assert 'this user wrote no journal entries', which is not the same claim as 'this build has no journal'.

workouts.description: Manually logged workouts. Distinct from the top-level `workouts` array, which holds ingested workout SESSIONS. A user who logs a run by hand and also wears a watch legitimately has both.

deletions.description: Tombstones: rows present in this bundle that carry a deleted_at. Deletion is recorded, not enacted by omission — a consumer syncing against a prior bundle needs to know a record went away rather than infer it from absence (§22.6).

config.description: The user's own export configuration, included so a backup restores settings rather than only data. Absent — not empty — when the emitting path did not supply it; an empty object would claim the user has no templates.

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 with a NUMERIC offset, rendered in the record's own timezone so the offset is carried rather than normalized to UTC. 'Z' is never emitted; a zero offset renders as +00:00 (§22.1).

timezone.description: IANA tz id at measurement (e.g. Asia/Dubai). The basis for day-boundary attribution.

ingestion_path.description: How the datum entered BADAN. 'vendor' is reserved for direct vendor/broker ingestion.

quality_flag.description: Honest annotations that travel with a datum. 'sampleData' marks a row fabricated by explore-with-sample-data mode — nobody measured it.

granularity.description: The time resolution a value describes. 'raw' is an as-measured reading. Null when the row's window is not a whole calendar unit — an arbitrary-length interval has no honest granularity, and a rounded-off guess would be worse than an absent one.

aggregation_method.description: How underlying readings were combined. 'none' asserts the value is a single reading (or an algorithm output that is not an aggregation of like readings) — it is an answer, not a missing one. Null is the missing one.

value_type.description: raw | aggregate | derived. With is_derived, the pair is what makes I5 checkable by a consumer that has flattened the arrays.

provenance.description: Embedded on the row itself, never a join (I1/D-3). A record without provenance is a bug, not a shortcut.

source_app.description: Bundle/package id of the app that produced the record.

external_id.description: The upstream system's own id — the idempotency key for re-ingest.

ingested_at.description: When BADAN stored it. The incremental-export cursor is the max of this field (§22.6), which is why a backfilled row still appears in a later delta run.

suppressed_by.description: record_id of the winning record when dedup suppressed this row. Suppression is reversible and journaled; it is never a deletion (I3).

value.description: The stored value, always in the metric's canonical unit. Unlike CSV's `value` column, the bundle does not apply a display unit profile — it publishes the canonical number plus what the source actually reported, and lets the consumer convert.

original_value.description: The value exactly as the source reported it.

coverage.description: 0–1 fraction of the window actually covered by underlying readings. Below 1 means the aggregate is over a partial window, which is a data-quality fact the consumer needs and BADAN does not silently backfill.

local_night.description: YYYY-MM-DD attribution key computed in the record's own timezone. This is what makes 'last night' survive DST and a post-midnight bedtime.

merged_from.description: record_ids of the raw sessions dedup combined into this one — the lineage the provenance sheet renders.

workout.description: A workout episode as a parent object. `strength_sets` from the plan's §22.2 sketch is NOT emitted: BADAN has no strength-set entity yet, and an empty array would claim the user recorded no sets rather than that the feature does not exist. It is reserved, not silently dropped.

record_id.description: The session ULID. Route filenames are derived from it (§22.4).

activity_type.description: A stable BADAN slug, never a platform's numeric enum value.

totals.description: The totals the SOURCE reported. Absent keys stay absent and are never coerced to zero: '0 kcal' and 'not recorded' are different claims. KNOWN PLATFORM DIVERGENCE: energy appears as `energy_kcal` from iOS and `energy_kj` from Android, because the two builds' WorkoutTotals landed on different stored units in EPIC-03. Exactly one of the two keys appears, and the key names the unit — a consumer must read whichever is present rather than assume. This is declared rather than papered over with a conversion, which would introduce float residue into a lineage record; see packages/fixtures/export/README.md knownDivergences.

energy_kcal.description: iOS only — see the divergence note above.

energy_kj.description: Android only — see the divergence note above.

hr_series_ref.description: A QUERY DESCRIPTOR into raw_samples, never a copy of the series. Absent when no HR linkage was recorded. Resolve it by selecting raw_samples where metric_id matches and start_at falls in [start_at, end_at]. KNOWN PLATFORM DIVERGENCE: only iOS can emit this today — Android's WorkoutDetail has no hrSeriesRef field, so an Android bundle omits the key even for a workout that has an HR series in raw_samples. Declared in packages/fixtures/export/README.md.

route_ref.description: Filename of the workout's GPX trace inside the artifact (§22.4). Location data gates independently of every other health class: this key is absent unless the export was built with the explicit route opt-in, and it is never present in a Quick Export.

source_workout_id.description: The platform's own workout id, so an exported workout correlates against Apple Health / Health Connect without the reader knowing how BADAN composes external ids.

detail_version.description: Version of the typed workout payload the row was read from. iOS stores it as an integer and Android as this string; both render into this one spelling so the bundle does not leak which platform wrote it.

period_key.description: day:YYYY-MM-DD | week:YYYY-Www | month:YYYY-MM | year:YYYY | session:<ulid>. granularity is read from this prefix, which is why it is null for a session-keyed value.

aggregation_method.description: 'none' on every derived value today: an algorithm output is not an aggregation of like readings, and claiming 'mean' would misdescribe how the number was produced. The algorithm's own composition is published in docs/algorithms/ and keyed by algorithm_id.

provisional.description: True while the inputs are too thin to be honest about. A provisional value is published, not hidden — hiding it would make the app look more certain than it is.

input_manifest_ref.description: Id of the input manifest listing the records this value was computed from.

baseline.description: A materialized personal-normal band. Timestamps render at +00:00 because a baseline spans many days and has no single measurement timezone to be faithful to.

low_detail.description: True for a 'quick calories' entry — honestly flagged rather than presented as a measured macro breakdown.

hydration_log.description: The `logs.hydration` block (EPIC-38 / §9.14). Present only when the export caught at least one drink. REDACTION is structural, not blanked: the default export withholds `note` (the key is absent from every entry) and the `redaction` object names every field a default file leaves out (§7A.1). The hydration CSV set (hydration_entries.csv etc.) carries the same rows and a byte-identical redaction manifest.

summaries.description: Per-local-day rollups with a frozen goal snapshot. Manual/imported/estimated totals are kept separate (I5) so an imported or estimated volume is never silently blended into what the user logged; only manual is populated this phase.

beverages.description: The custom beverage definitions the exported entries reference, so a reader can name each drink without the app or a separate catalog. Built-ins are not repeated here.

sources.description: The provenance apps/paths the entries came from, aggregated and sorted — the hydration-scoped answer to 'where did this come from' (I1), matching hydration_sources.csv.

hydration_redaction.description: The machine-readable statement of what a default hydration export leaves out (§7A.1). `notes_included` is false in a default export; `excluded_by_default` lists `note` (while withheld) plus the contexts this phase never models at all (fasting/cycle/pregnancy/location/reminder history), so the omission is disclosed rather than invisible.

hydration_entry.description: One logged drink from the append-first revision ledger (§9.14). A volume is always canonical mL — a fluid type is a display/grouping category, NEVER a hydration weight, so 500 mL of coffee is 500 mL exactly like water (§7A.1). `note` is present ONLY when the export explicitly opted notes in; a default export omits the key entirely.

original_id.description: The stable identity of the logical drink across every revision. Equal to record_id for an un-revised entry.

supersedes.description: record_id of the revision this one replaces; null for an original (I2 append-never-overwrite).

fluid_type.description: Open-vocabulary category key (water, coffee, tea, …) for grouping/display only — never a hydration multiplier.

note.description: Free-text note. Structurally redacted from a default export: the key is absent unless notes were explicitly opted in, never present-but-blank.

hydration_summary.description: A day's hydration rollup with a frozen goal snapshot: raising a goal next month does not retroactively mark last month's days as missed (§9.14). value_type is 'derived' — this is a computed rollup, physically separable from the raw entries (I5).

day_key.description: Local calendar day, YYYY-MM-DD, computed in `timezone`.

goal_target_ml.description: The snapshotted target, or null for a no-goal day (equal-status, never 0).

goal_progress_pct.description: Progress against the snapshotted target, or null for a no-goal day — a percentage of nothing is the streak-guilt framing §7A.1 rejects, so it is null, never 0.

hydration_goal.description: A hydration goal. `none` is a first-class, equal-status value — tracking without a target, never nagged (§7A.1) — so `target_ml` is null exactly when `kind` is `none`. `day_type` is a user-authored label (nothing infers it); null is the default goal.

hydration_beverage.description: A user-added beverage definition referenced by an exported entry. caffeine/alcohol/electrolyte are DISPLAY METADATA ONLY — carried so a reader sees the catalog fact, never read into a hydration total or a 'net hydration' multiplier (§7A.1 Reject).

manifest.description: The §22.5 manifest contract, embedded so the artifact is reproducible from its own description (D-8). The standalone manifest.json written alongside a CSV export carries the same fields.

scope.description: Full echo of the scope that produced this artifact. A null list means 'all', which is not the same as an empty list.

row_counts.description: Rows actually serialized per top-level array, counted by the writer from what it emitted rather than from what it was handed. Makes truncation detectable.

checksums.description: sha256 per file. Always describes the PLAINTEXT content, whether or not the artifact was encrypted on the way to disk. A self-contained bundle cannot checksum itself, so the bundle's own sha is recorded on the export job, not here.

sample_data_row_count.description: How many rows in THIS artifact were fabricated by sample/demo mode. Counted from the rows' own quality flags, not from an app-level demo switch, so it stays true for a store holding both kinds.

destination.description: Where the artifact was written, as name and kind ONLY. Credentials, tokens, account identifiers and secret-bearing paths are never recorded here — a manifest travels with the file it describes.
